BCRA's September data show NPLs and default probability falling, so the credit lines are unlikely to be cut. Guidance is normally given on the call, which is on 2026-11-30 after the exit window, so the window most likely sees the numbers without a new guide.

evidence.text: BCRA's Informe sobre Bancos for September 2026, published 2026-11-20, puts system Q3 ROA at 0.8% annualised (ROE 3.4%), against a Q2 ROA of 2.5% in its June report. The domestic private bank group ('EFB priv. nac.', which includes Macro) shows a 3-month ROA falling from about 1.4% in July to about 0.5% in September (Chart 17). The BCRA blames a lower 'margen financiero integral', partly offset by lower loan-loss charges, which fell as irregular loans dropped to 7.50% (families 12.20%, down 0.61pp). This is a broad series that contains Macro's own quarter and points to a peso miss against the Bloomberg consensus of ARS 219.5bn, which sits above Macro's Q2 206.8bn.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a 31.5% EPS beat traded -1.6% after hours. Q4 2025: profit 39% below the Bloomberg consensus (Bloomberg Linea, 'Banco Macro vuelve al verde pero no alcanza estimaciones'); that reaction was not sourced. On 2026-11-24 GGAL fell about 1% on a roughly 12% consensus miss.
evidence.why_not_priced: The consensus is visibly above Q2 (219.5 against 206.8bn) and has not been rebuilt on this series. If the market had fully priced it, the sell-side numbers would have converged down; Citi's 188.5bn and Goldman's -19% predate the 11-20 BCRA release. Part of it is priced anyway: BMA fell 7.65% in the 5 sessions spanning the BCRA release and the peer prints.
evidence.independence: Peer prints from separate issuer documents point the same way: BBAR's 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000913059/000129281426005393/bbarpr3q26_6k.htm), SUPV (https://www.riotimesonline.com/grupo-supervielle-q3-earnings-2026/) and GGAL (https://www.rava.com/noticias?ticker=GGAL_US). The BCRA aggregate contains those banks, so this finding and the peer findings share a common driver and are sized with that overlap in mind. Macro has the group's highest capital (CET1 28.4% per Goldman), and less leverage means less ROE sensitivity to margin.
evidence.link: Macro is one of the banks inside the 'EFB privados nacionales' group the series aggregates.

evidence.text: BBVA Argentina's 3Q26 6-K (2026-11-24) reports inflation-adjusted net income of AR$58.9bn, -57.7% QoQ, with ROE 4.9% against 12.2%, total NIM 15.1% against 18.2%, and fair-value income on government securities AR$16.4bn against 34.2bn. Citi had estimated AR$124.5bn, 6% below a Bloomberg consensus near 132bn (iProfesional 2026-11-13), so BBAR missed by more than half, and Goldman's ROE forecast of 8.8%. The CFO expects 'an upward path in profits' from Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: BBAR's own reaction on 2026-11-25 was not found. BMA has not paid for reported-quarter beats (Q2 2026 -1.6% on a 31% beat).
evidence.why_not_priced: The BMA estimates were set on 2026-11-13, before this print, so the BMA consensus has not absorbed the size of BBAR's margin and securities shortfall. Because the BBAR release is public, much of it is already in BMA's 5-day -7.65%.
evidence.independence: The BCRA September report is a separate document on the same driver (margin compression). SUPV's NIM fell 20.3% to 16.0% (https://www.riotimesonline.com/grupo-supervielle-q3-earnings-2026/).
evidence.link: Both are large private Argentine universal banks under the same BCRA rate and reserve-requirement regime, with large peso government-securities books. Goldman forecasts Macro's NIM falling 17.6% to 16.3%, a smaller drop than BBAR's 18.2% to 15.1%.

evidence.text: Grupo Financiero Galicia reported 3Q26 net income of ARS 229.0bn on 2026-11-24, down 16% QoQ on a smaller financial margin, with NPLs down to 9.7%. Citi had forecast 272.5bn, 5% above the Bloomberg consensus (about 259.5bn), so GGAL missed consensus by about 12%. Its ADR fell more than 1%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: GGAL ADR fell more than 1% on the miss, 'in line with other Argentine banks' (Bloomberg Linea via Rava). This peer's market punished a consensus miss only mildly.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: a public print one day before Macro's. It supports a miss against the Bloomberg consensus, which was built before the peer prints, and it also shows how small the reaction to a consensus miss was (-1%). That damping is why it is sized small.
evidence.independence: BCRA series (separate document); the BBAR 6-K. The Galicia figures come from press summaries aggregated on Rava (Forbes Argentina, Bloomberg Linea, iProfesional), not from the GFG press release itself.
evidence.link: The largest private domestic bank, in the same rate and reserve regime and the same BCRA group as Macro. Goldman forecast GGAL recurring profit -15% QoQ against -19% for Macro, so the actual -16% was in line with Goldman and below Citi and Bloomberg.

evidence.text: Grupo Supervielle's 3Q26 attributable net income was AR$6.8bn (2.2% ROE; AR$10.7bn excluding severance), half of Q2's 13.6bn. NIM fell 20.3% to 16.0% and net financial income fell 22.4%. Citi had forecast AR$28.3bn, 15% below a consensus near 33bn, so SUPV missed by about 75%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: SUPV's stock reaction on 2026-11-16/17 was not found.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public since 2026-11-16, before the Citi and Goldman previews were widely circulated (13 Nov) and before the BCRA release. It mostly confirms the system-wide margin squeeze, which BMA's 20-day -17% already reflects.
evidence.independence: Same driver as the BBAR and BCRA findings, so it is sized smallest of the three peers.
evidence.link: Smaller private domestic bank in the same rate regime. It is more retail and consumer-credit heavy than Macro and has a much thinner capital base (CET1 13.5% against Macro's 28.4%), so the read-through on margin is partial.

evidence.text: The Bloomberg consensus for Macro's 3Q26 net income (ARS 219.5bn, as of 2026-11-13) sits above Q2's reported 206.8bn, while Citi has 188.5bn, the largest peso gap to consensus of any bank Citi covers, and Goldman has recurring profit -19% real QoQ. The headline consensus is stale against the two broker previews.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025: profit 39% below the Bloomberg consensus (Bloomberg Linea); that reaction was not sourced. Q2 2026: a beat traded -1.6%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Headline screens will show a miss against 219.5bn. The buy-side reading the Citi and Goldman notes expects less, which is why this is capped small: the bar is disputed between sources (Chartmill implies about 200bn).
evidence.independence: Chartmill estimate (ARS 3,127 per ADR, about 200bn), from a search snippet only: https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/BMA/estimates

evidence.text: On 2026-08-19 management guided FY2026 reported ROE to 9-10% (adjusted about 12%) after Q1 at 10% and Q2 at 13.4%. That arithmetic implies a second-half ROE of roughly 7-8%, about ARS 110-130bn a quarter on an equity base near ARS 6.2tn (inferred from Q2's 206.8bn at 13.4%). A Q3 well below the Bloomberg 219.5bn would therefore sit inside what the company itself guided.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide changes on the Q2 call (loans cut to 2-5% from 15-20%, ROE guide raised) came with a -1.6% after-hours reaction and a slide from $75 to $50 since.
evidence.why_not_priced: A consensus of 219.5bn is visibly inconsistent with the company's own 9-10% reported ROE guide. Had the street priced the guide, the consensus would sit near 130-170bn and a 'miss' headline would not be in prospect. The equity base and the H2 split are this hunter's arithmetic on a transcript summary, not a company figure, hence the small size.
evidence.independence: Goldman's ROE 11.2% forecast sits between the guide-implied rate and consensus (iProfesional 2026-11-13).

evidence.text: Expectations are already low. BMA trades at $49.79, its 52-week low, 52% below the 52-week high, -17.3% over 20 days and -7.65% over 5 days. That is about 49% of the $100.71 Bloomberg consensus target and below every cut target (UBS $90 on 10-19, Goldman $95 on 11-13). Citi and Goldman both name Macro their only buy among Argentine banks. The 5-day fall covered the SUPV, BCRA, GGAL and BBAR releases, so a sector-wide Q3 miss is substantially in the price.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer GGAL fell only about 1% on its 12% consensus miss on 11-24, the day after a similar de-rating.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the price itself: what is priced is a sector margin miss. The finding says the bar the ADR holds is below the headline consensus, so a print near the broker numbers can hold or lift the stock. If the market were not braced, BMA would not have fallen 7.65% across the peer-print week.
evidence.independence: Sealed baseline tape (run-up fields); Goldman target cut on 2026-11-13 (https://www.iprofesional.com/finanzas/468851-wall-street-recomienda-una-sola-accion-entre-los-bancos-argentinos).

evidence.text: Banco Macro's board approved a buyback on 2026-10-28 of up to 20M Class B shares (Ps.160bn cap, max Ps.10,700, 45 calendar days, so it runs to about mid-December). It has bought on most sessions since 2026-10-30: 503,318 shares on 10-30, 294,214 on 11-11, 536,223 and 737,916 in the week of 11-17, 78,138 on 11-20, and 430,000 disclosed 11-24. Panabee tallies about 3.0M shares for Ps.28.6bn through 11-24, under 20% of the cap. The cap is about US$100m at about 1,600 ARS/USD, roughly 3% of market capitalisation, and it can keep buying through the window.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent on the reaction found. BMA has kept falling while the buyback ran (about -21% since 10-19).
evidence.why_not_priced: The program is public, but its remaining capacity (over 80% unspent) is a live bid into a thin post-Thanksgiving half-day. Buenos Aires trades Thursday 11-26 while New York is shut, and the buyback can absorb local selling that would otherwise arbitrage into the ADR on Friday. Had it been fully priced, the stock would not be at a fresh 52-week low.
evidence.independence: Execution disclosures via https://www.panabee.com/news/macro-bank-repurchases-294-thousand-shares-for-ps-2-8-billion (2026-11-24) and the Rava BMA news feed (https://www.rava.com/noticias?page=1&ticker=BMA).

evidence.text: Inside the quarter-close window, on 2026-10-28, about four weeks after Q3 closed and with the quarter's numbers largely in hand, Macro's board stated that the share price 'does not adequately reflect the value of its assets or its capacity to generate results' and committed up to Ps.160bn of capital. No other mid-quarter operating statement was found.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent found.
evidence.why_not_priced: Boards rarely spend excess capital on buybacks just before a disastrous quarter they already know about, so the act is weak evidence against a BBAR-style collapse. The stock's continued fall shows the market has not read it that way. Sized small because it is an inference from behaviour, not a figure.
evidence.independence: Shares one corporate act with the buyback finding (capital), which counts the bid. This finding counts only the information content, and the sizes are kept apart and small for that reason.

evidence.text: Citi raised its local target for Macro to ARS 15,500 from 9,680 (buy) while forecasting a below-consensus Q3. Goldman cut its ADR target to $95 from $110 while calling Macro's capital (CET1 28.4%) and asset quality the strongest of the three banks it covers. Both picked Macro as the one bank to own into the prints.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: not found
evidence.why_not_priced: Wire-level and largely priced. The sell-side owns a below-consensus Q3 and stays positive, so a miss against Bloomberg is less likely to trigger downgrades in the window.
evidence.independence: Shares a document with the consensus_bar finding; the two read different lines (the bar against the stance).

evidence.text: BMA's last print reaction shows it sells good quarters: on 2026-08-19 a 31.5% EPS beat ($1.92 against $1.46) traded -1.62% after hours ($75.22 to $74), and the stock has since lost a third.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat sold -1.6%; the baseline's 8 'moves' are buyback 6-Ks, not prints, and were not used.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a reaction function, not a fact the price lacks. It caps the upside of a beat and is filed so the judges can weigh it.
evidence.independence: GGAL's muted -1% on a miss (Rava, 2026-11-24) suggests the sector's print reactions are damped both ways and that macro drives these ADRs.

evidence.text: The 3Q26 conference call is on 2026-11-30 at 11:00 New York. On 2026-08-19 management said it needs 'at least one more quarter' before giving 2027 loan guidance, so the 2027 guide (loan growth, ROE, any dividend or buyback renewal) most likely arrives on that call, after the exit window closes on 2026-11-27. Peers' tone is cautious: SUPV cut its loan target at every report and BBAR noted 'signs of deterioration' in the macro.
The buyback's 45-day period ends around 2026-12-13/14, and renewal or extension is at the board's discretion.
Investing.com item dated 2026-11-04: 'Grupo Financiero Galicia ADR no alcanza por 0,12$ las previsiones de BPA en el tercer trimestre'.
The baseline's 'reaction history' (8 moves, median 3.08%) used as an earnings base rate.
Late-October Argentine macro sell-off (country risk about 745 after Brazil's election, Fed hike expectations, weak activity).
Q4 2025 profit 39% below the Bloomberg consensus.
Macro 3Q26 release or CNV local financial statements before the ADR release: not found (IR page lists the release as upcoming, after the close 2026-11-25).

Mid-quarter statements: no operating commentary (conference remarks, reaffirmation, pre-release) found after the 2Q26 call of 2026-08-19. The only management statement is the buyback rationale of 2026-10-28, which is filed as a finding.
BBAR and SUPV stock reactions to their 3Q26 prints: not found.
Sector ETF (ARGT) 5-day and 20-day returns: not sourced.
4Q26 and FY2026/27 street net income for Macro: not found.
October or November 2026 FINRA short-interest settlement for BMA: not found (latest 2026-09-30).
Status of Macro's US$400m bond reported as maturing November 2026: only an undated reference in a search summary, no primary source found.
BCRA bank-level (per-entity) September P&L for Macro: not reached; only the group aggregate in the Informe sobre Bancos.

evidence.text: Qfin, the largest US-listed peer in the same China consumer-credit facilitation channel, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-24 after FINV last spoke. It beat a lowered bar, with non-GAAP net income of RMB416.5m against a guide of 400-500m. It then guided Q4 net income to RMB210-310m (non-GAAP 250-350m, down 67-77% year on year), reported a 90+ day delinquency of 2.50%, day-1 delinquency of 5.8% and loan volume down 40.6% year on year, and the CEO cited 'clear erosion in risk performance', an 'industry-wide liquidity squeeze' and regulation persisting into 2027. QFIN fell 11.2% on 2026-11-25. The read-through is that FINV's Q4 and FY commentary is likely to show the same deterioration.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: FINV fell 15.4% after Q2 2026 on the 'lower part' FY guide and the warned Q3 China contraction (2026-08-28). QFIN's Q3 2025 print slid 13% after hours, as did FINV's Q3 2025 (-13.9% on 2025-11-20).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: FINV fell 4.6% on 11-25 against QFIN's -11.2%, so the full read-through is not in FINV's price. If it were fully priced, FINV would have matched QFIN's move or its implied move would have widened. The preview implied move fell from 23.1% to 11.8%.
evidence.independence: Qfin's own 2026-11-16 preview reported first-payment defaults up about 20% month on month in August and funding costs up about 25bp (https://finviz.com/news/423403/qfins-profit-floor-faces-its-first-test-as-credit-stress-and-funding-costs-bite). That is the same company, so it is not independent of this finding. FINV's own Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15496818263843840) points the same way.
evidence.link: Same business, regulation and funding channel. Both facilitate unsecured consumer loans for Chinese bank and trust partners under the NFRA notice effective 2025-10-01 and the 2026 debt-collection crackdown. China is about 70% of FINV's revenue (overseas was 27-30% in H1 2026). FINV's own Q2 call cited the same funding tightening and collection-capacity squeeze. Customers and lenders overlap at the industry level, but no shared-customer figure was found.

evidence.text: FINV's FY2026 revenue guide is RMB11.5-12.9bn, at the 'lower part'. The street's average is already below the low end at RMB11.31bn (range 10.9-11.6bn; EPS RMB5.32, down 47.6%). The H2 revenue the street implies (about 4.70bn against H1 of 6.61bn) means a formal cut to about 11.0-11.5bn would match expectations. Only a cut below about RMB10.9bn, or a Q4 profit outlook as steep as Qfin's, is new negative information.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance moved the stock at the last two prints: -15.4% on 2026-08-28 on the 'lower part' language, and +10.2% on 2026-05-26 with a reaffirmed guide plus a new $150m buyback.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street's figure is already below the guide, so a cut to that level is priced. What is not priced is how deep the cut goes and what the Q4 profit trajectory looks like after Qfin's 2026-11-24 data point. If a deep cut were priced, the stock would have fallen as far as QFIN on 11-25.
evidence.independence: Company guide: https://www.financialcontent.com/article/gnwcq-2026-8-27-finvolution-group-reports-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results . The Lexin Q3 2026 warning of a possible net loss (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/LexinFintech+Reports+Second+Quarter+2026+Unaudited+Financial+Results+and+Updates+Dividend+Policy) is an independent peer pointing the same way.

evidence.text: On the Q2 call (2026-08-27) FINV said China volume was 'down around 50% in July', early risk indicators were 'up around 20% versus the second quarter', funding cost rose 30bp to 3.7% with 'further upward pressure' expected, and the collection crackdown hurt recovery efficiency. Q3 provisions and margin should therefore be weaker than Q2, which had net profit of RMB426.8m. The company has already told the market this, so the item sits inside guidance.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The reported quarter has mattered less than the guide: Q2 2026 net profit down 43% was absorbed into a guide-driven -15.4%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is largely priced, because it is the company's own public warning. What is left is the size of the credit-cost step-up, which has no quarterly consensus to compare against. If the market had underestimated it, the stock would not have held a 4.6% loss against QFIN's 11%.
evidence.independence: Qfin reported day-1 delinquency of 5.8% and 90+ day delinquency of 2.50% in Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001741530/000110465926131684/tm2630464d1_ex99-1.htm). That source is shared with the first finding.

evidence.text: FINV trades below its cash. Cash plus short-term investments were RMB6.42bn (US$946m) at 2026-06-30, and management cited RMB7.5bn of cash plus about RMB5bn of highly liquid assets on the call. The market cap is about US$556m (roughly 238m ADS, inferred from 5.0m short shares being 2.1% of shares outstanding, × $2.335). The company has a $150m buyback authorised from 2026-05-30 to 2028-05-29 and bought $66.8m in H1. The Q3 release normally discloses the buyback amount, and any acceleration or new return at this valuation is a long-side catalyst.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print, announced with the new $150m buyback, rose 10.2% (2026-05-26; Simply Wall St notes about +15% after the news).
evidence.why_not_priced: The valuation is visible, but the market has looked through it through a 62% drawdown. The new information is the Q3 repurchase pace, which is not public until the release. If an acceleration were priced, the stock would not be at a fresh 52-week low.
evidence.independence: Buyback programme: https://finviz.com/news/356760/finvolution-group-announces-new-share-repurchase-program-of-up-to-us150-million . The share count is my inference from https://equibles.com/stocks/finv/shortinterest , so it is a proxy.

evidence.text: The setup into the print is washed out. The stock is down 10.5% over 5 days and 17.5% over 20 days to a 52-week low, 62% below its high and about 58% below the mean target of $5.61. The implied move has compressed to about 11.8% from 23.1% before the last print. The bar the price holds is low, which gives the reaction some asymmetry if the guide is only 'at street'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: A depressed setup has not protected this name: Q3 2025 (-13.9%) and Q2 2026 (-15.4%) both fell further.
evidence.why_not_priced: This item describes the price, so it is priced by definition. What it adds is how the next session reacts, and that asymmetry is the bet. Weekly peer moves of -6% to -15% show the drawdown is sector-wide, not FINV-specific.
evidence.independence: Baseline tape (run-up fields) and https://www.investing.com/equities/ppdai-consensus-estimates for targets.

evidence.text: Indonesia's OJK P2P lending data for September 2026 shows the industry's 90+ day default rate (TWP90) at 5.36%, up from 4.73% in August and above OJK's 5% threshold, with outstanding-loan growth slowing to 17.0% year on year from 22.1%. FINV's overseas business (Indonesia via AdaKami, plus the Philippines) is 27-30% of revenue and was its growth offset. This points to higher overseas credit costs in Q3 and Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The overseas segment has been the positive offset in recent prints (Q2 overseas operating profit more than doubled); no reaction to an overseas miss is on record.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is local-language industry data that the US sell-side previews do not cite. If it were priced, the overseas 'growth offset' narrative would already be discounted, but the targets still lean on it.
evidence.independence: https://keuangan.kontan.co.id/news/pembiayaan-fintech-lending-tumbuh-1702-per-september-2026-twp90-tembus-536 (different outlet, same OJK data). This is a macro proxy, not company data.
evidence.link: AdaKami is FINV's OJK-licensed Indonesian P2P platform. Overseas revenue was RMB930m in Q2 (27% of the total). No AdaKami-specific figure was found.

evidence.text: Chinese banks are cutting their online-platform partnerships. Jilin Yillion Bank went from 56 customer-acquisition partners in November 2024 to 10 in July 2026. Online-marketing measures for financial products took effect on 30 September, and regulators told e-commerce apps on 21 September to stop selling loans. Funding and traffic stay tight into Q4. China Daily also expects leading platforms to gain share as smaller ones exit.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Regulatory tightening drove the 2026 de-rating across the group; FINV's guide-driven -15.4% in August cited funding tightening.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced in the sector drawdown. What remains is whether the funding squeeze FINV said would last 'one or two quarters' extends into Q4.
evidence.independence: Sixth Tone on e-commerce lending (https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019049/China Tells E-Commerce Apps to Stop Selling Loans). Caixin 2026-09-10 calls FINV 'relatively resilient' (https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-09-10/chinas-online-lenders-see-profits-plunge-as-new-rules-bite-102483449.html).

evidence.text: FINV is the relative survivor of its group. In H1 2026 revenue fell about 6% and profit about 43%, against Qfin's revenue -25%, Jiayin's first interim loss (Q2 volume RMB9.5bn), X Financial's Q2 volume -70% and Vcredit's -84%. Lexin guided a possible Q3 net loss. Peers trade at $0.25 (YRD, with an NYSE price notice) to $1.17 (JFIN). If competitors exit, leading platforms can take share and acquisition costs fall.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of FINV being rewarded for relative resilience; it has traded with the group.
evidence.why_not_priced: FINV still fell with the group on 11-25 (-4.6%) and over the week (-9.4%). If the market priced its relative position, it would have decoupled from Lexin and Qfin.
evidence.independence: Qfin's own Q3 2026 release mentions competitor exits cutting industry acquisition spend (https://finviz.com/news/423403/qfins-profit-floor-faces-its-first-test-as-credit-stress-and-funding-costs-bite). YRD price notice: https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=YRD
evidence.link: Same China loan-facilitation channel and regulation. The share-gain mechanism is that banks consolidate onto fewer platforms (China Daily 2026-10-22). No FINV-specific share figure was found.

evidence.text: Short interest rose 10.7% in the two weeks to 2026-11-13 (4.48m to 4.96m shares) and days to cover went from 4.45 to 7.60. About 3.8% of float is short, so new shorts are building into the print but the position is not crowded.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze history on record; float short has stayed in low single digits.
evidence.why_not_priced: Short interest is published with a lag. The building short is informational at most; at 3.8% of float it is too small to drive a squeeze.
evidence.independence: Finviz short float 3.82% (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=FINV).

evidence.text: Analyst targets have not moved since 2026-08-28 (Citi Hold $4.10, Jefferies Buy $4.70; mean $5.61, all at least 75% above spot), and the targets for a 'Strong Buy' consensus look stale. Post-print target cuts toward spot are likely and would land in the session.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Citi's downgrade landed on the -15.4% session in August.
evidence.why_not_priced: Stale targets are a known condition. The fact is small and mostly priced.
evidence.independence: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/finv/forecast/ (same actions).

session_conflict.note: the event date carries the volume spike, so the market reacted on that date and the print was bmo. If tagged amc, the recorded move is the day-after give-back and may carry the wrong sign.

history.basis: 6-K exhibit text matched results language (8 filings opened). Heuristic, not an item code: a 6-K carrying results language is very likely an earnings release but this is weaker than the 8-K item 2.02 path

event_plausibility.reason: inferred cadence of 63 days is too short to be an earnings cadence (quarterly is ~91, semi-annual ~182), so the 8 matched filings are not earnings -- most likely monthly operational updates caught by the 6-K text matcher. No cadence verdict is possible and the reaction history above should not be used as an earnings base rate. Confirm the date from a company source instead.

baseline.deadband_basis: half the median of 8 prior reactions, floored at 1.5%
baseline.deadband_note: A realised move inside this band is scored as no-direction rather than as a miss.
baseline.expected_move_basis: median historical reaction (no usable option chain)

baseline_quality.note: thin means there is no reliable statement of what the market priced, so a confident call on this name cannot be justified by the baseline.

Every size is capped small because of this.

The company stopped giving quantitative guidance. Stock +2.04% on the day (baseline). Earlier confirmed prints: Q1 2026 (05-27) -2.87%, Q4 2025 (03-25, Q1 guide RMB14.5-15.5bn) -26.19%, Q3 2025 (2025-11-20) -15.7%.

expectations.real_bar: The market is pricing an arb spread, not the quarter. To rise, the release has to signal the deal is progressing (committee advisers hired, or no hint of a lower price) or show earnings that make $6.03 look safe or bumpable. A bidder-friendly gloomy outlook widens the spread.

next_guide.company_current_guide: none. Quantitative guidance was withdrawn on the Q2 2026 call because of 'material uncertainties in the operating environment' (https://quartr.com/events/x-financial-xyf-q2-2026_F3mv2nw4)
next_guide.basis: Guidance was dropped at Q2, and the CEO's affiliate is now the bidder, so management has every incentive not to issue an upbeat outlook ahead of a negotiated price. I expect no guide, or a cautious qualitative one.

evidence.text: The controlling holder proposed on 2026-11-06 to take XYF private at $6.03/ADS cash, a 28.3% premium to the prior close. The bidder holds ~94% of votes and ~48% of shares (13D: 110.9m shares, 47.97% of class, with Class B at 20 votes). A special committee of three independent directors was formed on 2026-11-18. Spot $5.23 is 15.3% below the bid, so the stock trades as a wide-spread arb. The only in-window paths to a big move are a deal update with the release (definitive agreement: low probability, ~5%, roughly +12%) or a hint the bid is being cut or withdrawn (~2%, roughly -10%).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The proposal day itself moved +22.34% (11-06). The two later deal filings (AGM notice 11-16, special committee 11-19) moved -1.11% and -0.19% per baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: The proposal itself is priced. What is not priced is whether the release carries a process update: the 15.3% spread, near-flat 5d tape and lack of arb compression show the market assigns real doubt or a long timeline. If an update were expected, the spread would be narrowing into the print, not widening from 4.9%.
evidence.independence: The special committee 6-K, 2026-11-19 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1725033/000110465926129959/tm2630265d1_6k.htm), and BBT News on financing by bank debt plus rollover (https://www.bbtnews.com.cn/2026/1106/610644.shtml). Both describe the same proposal.

evidence.text: Q3 2026 loan volume is likely to shrink again from Q2's RMB11.63bn. Q2 was -20.5% QoQ and -70.2% YoY, and the company withdrew guidance. A 2026-09-27 industry piece says Chinese loan-facilitation platforms were broadly contracting under the new fee/APR rules, including a 2026 rule folding fees into an annualised cost (one of seven listed platforms growing). So revenue, near RMB994m in Q2, likely falls again QoQ. The shrink is the expected base case, with no guide to miss, and the deal anchor damps it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume/guide disappointments drove -15.7% (Q3'25) and -26.2% (Q4'25, weak Q1 guide) before the proposal. The Q2'26 volume at the low end of the guide got +2.04%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the deliberate shrink was flagged at Q2. If the market expected a re-acceleration, the stock would trade nearer the bid. Only the size of a further drop is open.
evidence.independence: Industry proxy, partly garbled page: https://stock.stockstar.com/IG2026092700002284.shtml (2026-09-27). Search summaries also cite 'of 7 listed platforms only one growing' at the end of Q3. Proxy only, not company-confirmed.

evidence.text: Credit improved in Q2: 31-60 day delinquency fell to 1.73% from 2.61% in Q1, and 91-180 day to 9.09% from 9.95%. The loan-receivable provision fell to ~RMB10.1m from ~RMB52.3m in Q1, and net income rose 23.8% QoQ to RMB47.0m. If the release continues, Q3 profit can rise QoQ even on lower volume, and a richer profit print makes the $6.03 (~0.2x Q2 book equity of RMB7.76bn, ~$1.14bn) look safer or bumpable.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's provision-driven profit uptick with the low-end volume print got +2.04%.
evidence.why_not_priced: With no consensus and one stale analyst, nobody publishes a Q3 credit or profit estimate. The deal anchor means even a good number moves the spread only a little. If priced as a bump catalyst, the spread would be narrower than 15%.
evidence.independence: Same document as the volume finding (Q2 release), so two readings of one document on different lines. The CEO called the delinquency improvement 'constructive' but said 91-180 remains elevated.

evidence.text: Since the 11-06 proposal the stock has slid from $5.75 to $5.23 (-9%), widening the spread to the $6.03 bid from 4.9% to 15.3%. That is not explained by any filing: the only later 6-Ks are the AGM notice (no proposals) and the special committee. The market prices material doubt or a long timeline. A routine release that confirms the process is under way, without signalling a price cut, can narrow that slightly.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print under a pending bid.
evidence.why_not_priced: The spread is the price of the doubt, so this finding only says that doubt leaves room in both directions. A sized-up compression is not justified without a document.
evidence.independence: Baseline tape (spot 5.23 as of 2026-11-25, 5d -0.95%). Yahoo shows the $5.50 close on 11-12 (search snippet).

evidence.text: The next guide is likely absent or cautious. Management withdrew quantitative guidance at Q2 and the bidder is the CEO's affiliate, so the outlook commentary is controlled by the buyer. A gloomy outlook (regulatory language already warns past profitability should not be assumed) supports the bidder's price and can widen the spread.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4'25 print with a weak Q1 guide fell 26.19%. The Q2'26 print that withdrew guidance rose 2.04%.
evidence.why_not_priced: No-guide is already the market's base case since Q2. Only a harsher-than-expected tone would move it, and the deal anchor caps that.
evidence.independence: The Q2 release's regulatory risk language (https://finviz.com/news/384651/x-financial-reports-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results) and the Q4'25 release's 'operating losses cannot be excluded' (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/955039/x-financial-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-unaudited-financial-results).

evidence.why_not_priced: Small: renewal is not expected by anyone tracking the bid. A surprise renewal would be mildly positive.
evidence.independence: The dividend cadence is in the Q4'25 release (record 2026-04-30) and the Q2'26 release (record 2026-09-10).
